name: Latte macchiato
caffeine: From the espresso marked into the milk, a single or a double; the milk adds none.

house.ask: Not printed on our menus: ask at lineup whether there is an espresso machine, whether the bar will make a latte macchiato, and at what price.

what: Milk stained with coffee, the reverse of a caffè macchiato. Steamed milk goes into a tall glass first and the espresso last, poured slowly, so it sits in layers: pale milk, a band of coffee, a cap of foam. Milkier than a latte, and served in glass so the layers show.
taste: Mostly warm, sweet milk, the coffee arriving in waves as you drink down through the layers.

steps: Size the pitcher to a warmed tall glass and steam only the milk you will pour.
Stretch a little longer than for a latte, spin glossy, cut near 135 to 140F (57 to 60C), and fill the glass.
Let it settle a moment so the foam rises, and pull a single or a double into a small jug.
Pour the shot slowly through the centre of the foam, so it settles in a band beneath.
make.ratio: More milk than a latte; the shot only marks it
make.dose: One or two shots of espresso; milk to fill
make.time: Shot 25 to 30 seconds; serve before layers blur
make.cup: Warmed tall glass, 8 to 12 oz, on a saucer

serve: On a saucer with a long spoon and a napkin, since the glass is hot to hold. Bring it straight from the machine so the layers show, and let the guest stir.
story: Macchiato means stained or marked. The caffè macchiato is espresso marked with milk; the latte macchiato turns it round. Chain menus sell a sweet syrup drink by a similar name, closer to a vanilla latte, so ask which a guest means: the three come in different glasses.
guest: A tall glass of steamed milk with espresso poured in last, so it sits in layers: milkier and gentler than a latte.
watch: Ask which macchiato the guest means: the short espresso, this tall glass, or the syrup drink.
A fast pour, or one from height, mixes the shot through and no layers form.
A guest who wants more coffee is better served by a latte or a flat white.

study: Pitcher, volume and the pour window

recall.prompt: How is a latte macchiato built, and in what order?
recall.answer: Steamed milk into a warmed tall glass first, left to settle, then a single or double espresso poured slowly through the foam to rest in a band beneath it. Milky, sweet and layered.

quiz.q: What does the Italian word macchiato mean?
quiz.explain: Macchiato means stained: espresso stained with milk, or here, milk stained with espresso.

quiz.q: In a latte macchiato, what goes into the glass last?
quiz.explain: Milk first, then the shot poured slowly through the foam, which is what makes the layers.

quiz.q: How does a latte macchiato differ from a caffè macchiato?
quiz.explain: The caffè macchiato is a short espresso with a mark of milk; the latte macchiato reverses it.
